status: SIGNED - author chose 'Fix collector, redo once' in the Claude Code session of 2026-10-25

discovery_path.what_happened: While the author-approved rerun results were being written into the prose, the singleton-sensitivity rows (truth-derived exact scores) showed identical primary and abstain-all scores for HLA-HD, arcasHLA and the vote. A truth-free inspection of the activated caller table then showed that every HLA-HD single-allele row (65 cells) carried HLA-HD's documented homozygous marker '-' as its second allele but had call_status 'partial', so it abstained under the primary policy.
discovery_path.truth_derived_information_seen: The registry and delta the author had approved, including the singleton-sensitivity scores that prompted the inspection. The defect itself was confirmed only from caller-output fields (raw alleles, call status, homozygosity basis).
discovery_path.cause: scripts/collect_development_rerun.py labelled an aggregate pair as a caller-native declaration only when the v3.5.0 aggregate already marked it callable; it never completed a non-callable single-allele row from the caller's own summary. The v3.5.0 aggregator marks those rows non-callable, so the signed native-declaration policy was not applied to HLA-HD (and could not be applied to arcasHLA).

decision.correction: The collector completes a non-callable single-allele row into a homozygous pair, labelled caller_native_declaration, when the caller's own summary declares it: always for HLA-HD ('-'), and for arcasHLA only when the sample's checksummed versions.yml records a release before 0.4.0 (unknown versions abstain). The completed pair must equal the summary's declared pair or collection stops. The abstain-all sensitivity table removes these declarations as before.
decision.scope: This restores the signed 2026-10-08 singleton policy; it changes no rule. Collection, activation and the single regeneration are repeated; the previous activation, its collection and its registry are kept as superseded provenance.
decision.approvals: decisions/20261025_rerun_registry_delta_approved.json and its identity-rows amendment bind registries computed from the defective inputs; they no longer authorize prose, and the corrected registry needs a new author approval.
decision.unchanged: Roster, release, endpoint, consensus rule, panels, multiplicity, singleton policy, outer folds and every analysis choice. Nothing is tuned against a truth-derived quantity.

authorization.signed: 2026-10-25, explicit author choice: 'Fix collector, redo once'
